title: FIND and SEARCH
explanation: Last lesson, every code had the same length, so you always knew where to cut. Names and emails are different lengths, so you need to **find** where to cut first, like the @ in an email or the space in a name. FIND and SEARCH tell you the position of a character, and you combine them with LEFT and MID.

tasks.prompt: In C2, find the position of the @ in Maya's email: =FIND("@", B2).
tasks.teach: **FIND(what, text)** gives the position of the first match. In maya.lee@wes.edu the @ is the **9th** character. Text you search for goes in quotes.

tasks.prompt: In D2, take everything before the @ to get the username: =LEFT(B2, FIND("@", B2) - 1). Then copy it down to D7.
tasks.teach: The username stops one character **before** the @, so take FIND's position minus 1. Putting FIND inside LEFT works for every email, whatever its length.
hints: =LEFT(B2, FIND("@", B2) - 1), then copy it down.
tasks.answer: =LEFT(B2, FIND("@", B2) - 1) in D2, then copy down to D7

tasks.prompt: In E2, take everything after the @ to get the school: =MID(B2, FIND("@", B2) + 1, 100). Then copy it down to E7.
tasks.teach: MID starts one character **after** the @. The 100 just means "take up to 100 characters", which is more than enough to reach the end.
hints: =MID(B2, FIND("@", B2) + 1, 100), then copy it down.
tasks.answer: =MID(B2, FIND("@", B2) + 1, 100) in E2, then copy down to E7

tasks.prompt: Same trick for names. In F2, take the first name: everything before the space. Then copy it down to F7.
hints: Find the space with FIND(" ", A2).
=LEFT(A2, FIND(" ", A2) - 1), then copy it down.
tasks.answer: =LEFT(A2, FIND(" ", A2) - 1) in F2, then copy down to F7

tasks.prompt: In G2, take the last name: everything after the space. Then copy it down to G7.
hints: Start one character after the space, like the school column.
=MID(A2, FIND(" ", A2) + 1, 100), then copy it down.
tasks.answer: =MID(A2, FIND(" ", A2) + 1, 100) in G2, then copy down to G7

tasks.prompt: Last one: FIND cares about capitals, SEARCH doesn't. In C9, use SEARCH to find "pro" in A9 (which says PRO in capitals).
tasks.teach: **FIND** is case-sensitive, so `FIND("pro", A9)` gives an error, because A9 says PRO. **SEARCH** works the same way but ignores capitals, so it finds it at position 11.

recap: FIND and SEARCH give the position of a character, and SEARCH ignores capitals. Combine them with LEFT and MID to split text at an @, a space or a comma, whatever its length.
